statement_record.book: Definition 4.1.1 admits three dualizations. Opposing BOTH categories gives nothing new: G : D^op ⟶ C^op is left adjoint to F : C^op ⟶ D^op iff F ⊣ G, so every left-adjoint theorem dualizes to a right-adjoint one. Opposing one side gives two genuinely new notions: F : C^op ⟶ D and G : D^op ⟶ C are MUTUALLY LEFT ADJOINT when D(Fc,d) ≅ C(Gd,c) naturally, and MUTUALLY RIGHT ADJOINT when D(d,Fc) ≅ C(c,Gd) naturally; the first comes with a pair of 'counits' GF ⇒ id_C, FG ⇒ id_D, the second with a pair of 'units' id_C ⇒ GF, id_D ⇒ FG (triangle identities in Exercise 4.4.i).
statement_record.intree: Opposite_Adjunction `(F : D ⟶ C) `(U : C ⟶ D) (A : F ⊣ U) : U^op ⊣ F^op — with (A^op)^op = A by reflexivity (Opposite_Adjunction_invol).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the THIRD dualization (both categories opposed) is formalized, and it is exactly the clause Riehl says yields nothing new. Neither of the two notions the definition actually introduces — mutually left adjoint (D(Fc,d) ≅ C(Gd,c)) and mutually right adjoint (D(d,Fc) ≅ C(c,Gd)) between contravariant functors — has any in-tree counterpart, nor do the associated paired units/counits.

gap: The definition itself is absent. The library has no class, definition, or instance for a pair of contravariant functors F : C^op ⟶ D, G : D^op ⟶ C carrying a natural iso D(Fc,d) ≅ C(Gd,c) (mutually left adjoint) or D(d,Fc) ≅ C(c,Gd) (mutually right adjoint), and none of the paired natural transformations (two counits GF ⇒ id_C, FG ⇒ id_D in the left case; two units id_C ⇒ GF, id_D ⇒ FG in the right case). Both notions ARE expressible with existing machinery — mutual left adjointness of (F,G) is the ordinary in-tree adjunction F ⊣ G^op between C^op and D, mutual right adjointness is F^op ⊣ G between C and D^op — but no in-tree statement records that translation, so nothing asserts the definition or its symmetry. The only in-tree assertion bearing on the item is the both-sides dualization Opposite_Adjunction, which is the degenerate case.

statement_record.book: Prop 4.4.4: let F : A ⟶ B be a functor such that for each b ∈ B there is an object Gb ∈ A and an isomorphism B(Fa,b) ≅ A(a,Gb) natural in a. Then there is a UNIQUE extension of the object assignment G to a functor G : B ⟶ A making the isomorphisms natural in b as well; consequently, if each B(F−,b) : A^op ⟶ Set is representable, the data assembles into an adjunction F ⊣ G. A dual criterion characterizes functors admitting a left adjoint. Proof by Yoneda applied to A(−,Gb) ⇒ A(−,Gb').
statement_record.intree: AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows (H : forall c : C, UniversalArrow c U) : Adjunction (LeftAdjointFunctorFromUniversalArrows H) U, where LeftAdjointFunctorFromUniversalArrows builds the functor with fmap the unique factorization delivered by ump_universal_arrows (∃! g, h ≈ fmap[U] g ∘ arrow), and UniversalArrowIsUniversalProperty identifies a universal arrow with a representation of d ↦ Hom_C(c, U d).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only ONE of the two orientations is stated, and it is the one Riehl relegates to the closing sentence ('a dual representability criterion characterizes functors admitting a LEFT adjoint'). In-tree the given functor is the RIGHT adjoint U and the constructed one the left adjoint F; Riehl's headline direction (F given, right adjoint G constructed from representations of B(F−,b)) has no in-tree statement. Uniqueness is also weaker in form: in-tree it is the pointwise ∃! of ump_universal_arrows on each mediating morphism, not a theorem that the functor structure extending the object assignment is unique.

gap: Two things are missing. (1) The primary orientation: there is no in-tree construction of a RIGHT adjoint from a family of representations of B(F−,b) : A^op ⟶ Set (equivalently, from terminal objects of the comma categories F ↓ b / couniversal arrows). rg finds no 'couniversal', no RightAdjointFunctor*, and Theory/Universal/Arrow.v's UniversalArrow is exclusively the initial-object-in-=(c) ↓ F form; the dual is obtainable by transporting through Adjunction/Opposite.v's Opposite_Adjunction, but no file does so. statement_record.book: Prop 4.4.6, for F : A × B ⟶ C. (i) If each F(a,−) : B ⟶ C has a right adjoint G_a, there is a UNIQUE bifunctor G : A^op × C ⟶ B with G(a,−) = G_a such that C(F(a,b),c) ≅ B(b,G(a,c)) is natural in all THREE variables. (ii) dually for F(−,b) with right adjoints H_b, giving H : B^op × C ⟶ A and C(F(a,b),c) ≅ A(a,H(b,c)) natural in all three. (iii) When both hold, G(−,c) : A^op ⟶ B and H(−,c) : B^op ⟶ A are mutually right adjoint.

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on three counts: (1) only ONE of the two transpositions is present (the right closure of − ⨂ y), so the triple (F,G,H) is never formed; (2) everything is stated for a single category with an endo-tensor F : C ∏ C ⟶ C, not for three possibly distinct categories A, B, C; (3) exp_iso is a family of hom-setoid isomorphisms indexed by (x,y,z) with no naturality field at all — naturality is recovered only piecemeal as derived lemmas (curry_comp_l, curry_comp, uncurry_comp), never as the single natural isomorphism the definition requires.
